observations:
Torah #68 is a short, tightly focused teaching — 11 lines, 3 dataset bechina edges, 6 dataset nodes. After exhaustive scanning of all bechina-language statements in the source text, no independent conceptual domain of 3+ explicitly bechina-linked concepts was found that is not already covered by the two proposed packages.

The four flagged additions (נפש, גבורות, כעס↔ממון at the root, עיר פרוצה) all attach to the existing packages:
  - נפש and גבורות extend Package 1 (Wealth and Holy Overflow), filling in the supernal root structure.
  - עיר פרוצה אין חומה extends Package 2 (Anger and Evil), providing the evil-side mirror for חומה.
  - The missing ממון↔כעס edge at the root-level is the bridge between Package 1 and Package 2; it connects the two existing packages rather than forming a new independent domain.

The Torah's argument follows a clear two-package structure with an eitza narrative connecting them:
  Stage 1 — The holy source of wealth [Package 1: good — ממון/שפע קדש/חומה/נפש]
  Stage 2 — The evil inversion: anger destroys the wall [Package 2: evil — כעס/רעה/עיר פרוצה]
  Eitza bridge — The Baal Davar converts descending shefa into anger: Package 1 → Package 2 (via the adversary's action).

The good/evil mirror structure is present and exact:
  Package 1 (holy): מָמוֹן is בְּחִינַת חוֹמָה (a protective wall)
  Package 2 (evil): כַּעַס is the קִלְקוּל הַחוֹמָה (ruination of the wall) = עִיר פְּרוּצָה (a breached city)
  Both descend from Gevurot/Tzafon — gold from north (Iyov 37) mirrors evil/anger from north (Yirmiyah 1).

No third domain was found. The concept of גְּבוּרוֹת (the Sefirah from which both descend) could theoretically be its own structural node, but Torah #68 contains only one bechina statement touching it (both descend from Gevurot) and it serves as the theological explanation for the Package 1–Package 2 identity, not as an independent domain with its own sub-cluster of 3+ bechina-connected concepts.
